questions.q: What incident does this lesson's retrospective trace the entire program back to?
options: A warehouse inventory mismatch at Harbor
The six-week UK GDPR data subject access request from Lesson 1, which surfaced conflicting order histories and reached the board
A failed Power BI dashboard refresh
An unrelated vendor contract dispute
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly closes the loop back to the Lesson 1 DSAR incident as the origin point for everything the program built.

questions.q: According to the lesson's first realistic caveat, how long would a real version of this program likely take, compared to the eighteen-lesson sequence?
options: Exactly eighteen days
Roughly twelve to twenty-four months, across multiple budget cycles
A single uninterrupted weekend
There is no difference; real programs move just as fast as this capstone
questions.explain: The lesson states explicitly that a real rollout spans twelve to twenty-four months and multiple budget cycles, unlike the continuous eighteen-lesson sequence.

questions.q: What does the lesson's 'politics' caveat warn about regarding decisions like Lesson 9's authoritative-source calls?
options: That such decisions are illegal without board approval
That domain owners never disagree with each other in practice
That a domain owner whose system 'loses' a decision often pushes back, and the operating model needs real executive backing to hold in that moment
That authoritative-source decisions are purely technical with no human factor
questions.explain: The lesson explains that decisions which land cleanly in this capstone would face real pushback in practice, requiring genuine executive backing for the operating model to hold.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say 'done' is the wrong word for a governance program, even a successful one?
options: Because the program fundamentally failed
Because the operating model keeps producing and correcting the glossary, CDE register, KPIs, and architecture going forward, rather than freezing them at Lesson 18
Because Lesson 18 is not actually the final lesson in Chapter 1
Because governance programs are legally required to run forever unchanged
questions.explain: The lesson ties this directly back to Lesson 12's operating model, which maintains every deliverable as ongoing work rather than a one-time, frozen output.

questions.q: What does this lesson say carries forward from the capstone into the career-preparation chapter that follows?
options: Nothing; the capstone and career chapters are unrelated
Only the final PowerPoint deck from Lesson 17
A demonstrable portfolio of real work — CDE scoring, ownership design, SQL quality checks, architecture, and executive communication — that a candidate can walk a hiring manager through
A requirement to repeat all eighteen lessons verbatim in an interview
questions.explain: The lesson frames the entire capstone as concrete portfolio evidence a candidate can describe and defend, directly setting up the career-preparation chapter that begins with Lesson 19.
